key_insight: LLM2R reframes 3D part assembly as one-shot sequence modeling with a pretrained decoder-only LLM, using summary tokens to capture whole-assembly context and predict all part poses in a single forward pass.
engineering_relevance: This matters for fracture and damage reassembly because it scales better to many fragments than pairwise or iterative methods, improving practical reconstruction of complex broken objects.
method: Point-BERT + Q-Former compress each part into geometric token blocks.
Concatenate all part blocks and process them with a causal LLM adapted via LoRA.
Add learnable summary tokens after the last part and fuse them in a part-aware pose head to predict SE(3) transforms.
evidence_signal: The paper reports state-of-the-art part accuracy and success on three PartNet categories, best rotation/translation errors and part accuracy on PartNeXt, and the fastest inference with lowest translation error on Breaking Bad, with especially large gains at 100 parts and strong zero-shot transfer.
watch_item: Because the backbone is causal, early part states cannot directly attend to later parts; the summary-token design mitigates this, but performance may still depend on token compression quality and the learned ordering of parts.
paper_title: LLM2R: From Large Language Models to 3D Reassemblers
